mainTopic: The joy of ט״ו באב and the vineyard dances, ending מסכת תענית with the future dance of the צדיקים.
overview: The משנה says ט״ו באב was one of the happiest days for the Jewish people, and the גמרא lists reasons why. The amud opens with the last words of one reason: הושע בן אלה let the people go up to ירושלים freely. רב מתנה adds that on this day the slain of ביתר were finally buried, and that is when the חכמים in יבנה set up the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב. רבה and רב יוסף say it was the day they stopped cutting wood for the מזבח, and a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול explains that after this date the sun is too weak to dry the wood. From then on the nights grow longer, so one who adds Torah learning at night adds life, and רב יוסף explains what happens to one who does not. The גמרא then goes back through the משנה: everyone borrowed white clothes so no poor girl would be embarrassed, the clothes needed טבילה, and unmarried men came to the vineyards to find a wife, while each group of girls praised its own strength. The מסכת ends with רבי אלעזר's picture of the צדיקים dancing around הקדוש ברוך הוא in גן עדן, followed by the הדרן for the פרק and the whole of מסכת תענית.

steps.title: End of the earlier reason: they may go up wherever they want
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the earlier reason: הושע בן אלה allowed the people to go up to whatever place they wished.
steps.simpleTranslation: …they may go up to whichever place they want.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a reason that began on the previous amud. הושע בן אלה removed the guards that kept people from going up to ירושלים and said, 'Let them go up wherever they want.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings of the Northern Kingdom had placed guards on the roads so the people could not go up to the בית המקדש. On ט״ו באב, הושע בן אלה took the guards away, and that freedom is one reason the day was joyful. This is the tail end of that reason, not a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: they shall go up (to a holy place)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the last part of a reason that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: to whichever (place) they wish, let them go up.
phrases.notes: Words of הושע בן אלה, who removed the guards on the roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reason about הושע בן אלה earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב is joyful because הושע בן אלה let the people go up freely.

steps.title: רב מתנה: the slain of ביתר were buried on this day
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה gives a new reason for the joy of ט״ו באב: it was the day the people killed at ביתר were finally allowed to be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It was the day that the people killed at ביתר were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, separate reason for why ט״ו באב is a happy day. רב מתנה says it was the day the dead of ביתר were finally buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the Romans destroyed ביתר, they would not let the Jews bury the dead for a long time. The day burial was finally allowed was a day of relief and thanks, and that explains the joy of ט״ו באב.

keyTerms.meaning: the people killed at ביתר (the city destroyed by the Romans)

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
(It was) the day that the slain of Beitar were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reason for the joy of ט״ו באב, in addition to the reason before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב was the day the slain of ביתר were brought to burial.

steps.title: The ברכה of הטוב והמטיב was set up at יבנה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה adds that on that same day the חכמים in יבנה set up the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב, with each phrase thanking ה׳ for a different kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מתנה said: On that same day, when the slain of ביתר were given over for burial, they set up in יבנה the ברכה 'Who is good and does good.' 'Who is good' – that the bodies did not rot. 'And does good' – that they were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה tells us something else that happened on that day: the חכמים in יבנה set up the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב. Each half of the ברכה matches a separate miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two kindnesses. First, the bodies did not rot even though they lay unburied for a long time; that is 'הטוב.' Second, the Jews were finally allowed to bury them; that is 'והמטיב.' This explains where the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: יבנה, the seat of the חכמים after the חורבן
'Who is good and does good' – the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב that we say every time we bentch.

phrases.english: And Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ יוֹם שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ הֲרוּגֵי בֵיתֵּר לִקְבוּרָה,
phrases.english: That same day that the slain of Beitar were given over for burial,
they instituted at Yavne (the blessing) 'Who is good and does good.'
'Who is good' – that they did not rot,
'and does good' – that they were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement by רב מתנה about the same event in ביתר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה of הטוב והמטיב was set up at יבנה on the day the slain of ביתר were buried: הטוב for the bodies not rotting, והמטיב for their burial.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the day they stopped cutting wood for the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף give another reason: ט״ו באב was the day they finished cutting wood for the fire on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: It was the day they stopped cutting wood for the altar fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another reason for the joy of ט״ו באב. Here רבה and רב יוסף agree: it was the day the wood-cutting for the מזבח ended for the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood for the מערכה, the fire on the מזבח, was cut during the hot months so it could dry. Finishing this important מצוה work was a reason to celebrate. The next step will explain why the cutting stopped on this particular date.

keyTerms.meaning: the arrangement of wood burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: (It is) Rabba and Rav Yosef who both say:
(It was) the day they stopped cutting wood for the altar arrangement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reason for ט״ו באב, separate from רב מתנה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב was the day they finished cutting wood for the מערכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains why the wood-cutting stopped on ט״ו באב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול backs up רבה and רב יוסף: after ט״ו באב the sun gets weaker, so newly cut wood would not dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: From ט״ו באב onward the sun's strength gets weaker, and they would not cut wood for the altar, because it would not dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support what רבה and רב יוסף said. It explains the reason behind the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood for the מזבח had to be dry. Wet wood could get wormy, and wormy wood is not fit for the מזבח. After ט״ו באב the sun is weaker, so new wood would not dry well, and that makes ט״ו באב the last day for cutting.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
From the fifteenth of Av onward
the strength of the sun weakens,
and they would not cut wood for the altar arrangement,
because they would not be dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה and רב יוסף with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that wood-cutting for the מערכה stopped on ט״ו באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול: after ט״ו באב the sun weakens and wood would not dry.

steps.title: רב מנשיא: it was called 'the day the axe breaks'
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא adds that people called ט״ו באב 'the day of breaking the axe,' since tree-cutting ended on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא said: And they called it 'the day the axe breaks.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא adds a detail to the wood-cutting reason: the day had a popular name, 'יום תבר מגל.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cutting was finished, the cutting tools were no longer needed, as if they were broken. The name shows how well known this end-of-cutting day was.

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:
And they called it 'the day of the breaking of the scythe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the popular name of the day to the wood-cutting reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב was known as יום תבר מגל.

steps.title: From now on, one who adds learning adds life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא teaches that from ט״ו באב onward, someone who adds Torah learning at night will have life added to him, and someone who does not add 'will be gathered.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From here onward, one who adds will have added to him, and one who does not add will be gathered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a lesson that follows from the date: the nights start getting longer, so a person should add Torah learning at night. It uses a strong phrase, 'יאסף.' The next step asks what it means, and רב יוסף answers in the step after that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sun weakens after ט״ו באב, the nights get longer, and there is more time to learn. A person who uses this extra night time to learn will have years added to his life. A person who does not add is warned with the word 'יאסף,' 'he will be gathered.'

keyTerms.meaning: one who adds (Torah learning at night)
will have added to him (more life)

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not say what to add. It means adding Torah learning at night, because the nights are getting longer.

phrases.english: From here onward,
phrases.notes: From ט״ו באב, when the nights lengthen.

phrases.english: one who adds (to his learning) – will have (life) added,
and one who does not add – will be gathered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the weakening of the sun mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ט״ו באב on, adding night learning adds life, and not adding brings 'gathering.'

steps.title: What does 'he will be gathered' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word יאסף means here.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he will be gathered' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the unclear word 'יאסף' from the last step. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'gathered' is vague. It could be a mild punishment, or it could mean something much stronger. The גמרא wants to know exactly what it means.

phrases.english: What is 'will be gathered'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the previous statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'יאסף' for one who does not add learning.

steps.title: רב יוסף: his mother will bury him
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that 'יאסף' means he will die young, so that his mother buries him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: His mother will bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. 'He will be gathered' means he will die so young that his own mother will bury him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Gathered' is a phrase used for dying ('gathered to his people'). רב יוסף sharpens it: he will die before his time, while his mother is still alive. This is the opposite of 'יוסיף,' getting years added to one's life.
steps.whatToRemember: ט״ו באב is joyful for several reasons: הושע בן אלה let the people go up freely, the slain of ביתר were buried (which is the source of הטוב והמטיב), and the wood-cutting for the מזבח ended. From this date the nights get longer, so a person should add Torah learning at night. Adding learning adds life, and not adding risks dying young.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
His mother will bury him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of יאסף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'יאסף' means he will die young, so that his mother buries him.

steps.title: Everyone borrowed white clothes so no one would be embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the daughters of Jerusalem going out in white. A ברייתא explains that everyone borrowed clothes from someone of lower rank, so a girl without her own white clothes would not be shamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On those days the daughters of ירושלים would go out' in borrowed white clothes. תנו רבנן: the king's daughter borrows from the כהן גדול's daughter. The כהן גדול's daughter borrows from the סגן's daughter. The סגן's daughter borrows from the משוח מלחמה's daughter. The משוח מלחמה's daughter borrows from a כהן הדיוט's daughter. And all of ישראל borrow from one another, so that the person who has nothing will not be embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the line about the daughters of Jerusalem. It then brings a ברייתא that explains the borrowing in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the borrowing was organized on purpose. Even the king's daughter, who surely owned white clothes, borrowed someone else's. Because every girl wore borrowed clothes, nobody could tell who was rich and who was poor, so the poor girl was not singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: the deputy of the כהן גדול
the כהן anointed to speak to the army before battle

steps.confusionAlert: The text shows a correction: the parentheses (יתבייש, 'be embarrassed') mark the old reading, and the square brackets [לבייש, 'to embarrass'] mark the corrected one. Read it as 'so as not to embarrass the one who has none.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of protecting a poor person's dignity. The rich adjusted their own behavior so the poor would not feel different.

phrases.english: 'As on them the daughters of Jerusalem,' etc.
phrases.notes: A quote of the משנה, used as a heading.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a ברייתא):

phrases.aramaic: בַּת מֶלֶךְ שׁוֹאֶלֶת מִבַּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: The king's daughter borrows from the High Priest's daughter,
the High Priest's daughter borrows from the deputy's daughter,
and the deputy's daughter borrows from the daughter of the priest anointed for war,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַת מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה — מִבַּת כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: and the daughter of the priest anointed for war borrows from an ordinary priest's daughter,
and all the Jewish people borrow from one another
so as not to embarrass
the one who does not have (her own).

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבָּהֶן בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of ט״ו באב and night learning, and returns to explain the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone borrowed white clothes from someone of lower rank, so the girl who had none would not be embarrassed.

steps.title: Borrowed clothes need immersion, even if stored folded
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says all the borrowed clothes needed טבילה. רבי אלעזר adds that this applies even to clothes that were folded away in a box.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: all the clothes require טבילה. רבי אלעזר said: this applies even if they were folded and lying in a box.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about immersing the clothes, and רבי אלעזר widens it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think clothes folded away in a box were surely untouched and still טהור, so they would not need טבילה. רבי אלעזר says they still need it. The rule covers every borrowed garment, with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: immersion in a מקוה to remove טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Here כלים does not mean dishes or utensils. It means the borrowed clothes.

phrases.english: All the garments require immersion.
Rabbi Elazar said:
Even if they are folded and lying in a box.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים טְעוּנִין טְבִילָה. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the משנה, moving from the borrowing to the purity of the borrowed clothes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowed garments need טבילה even when they were stored folded in a box.

steps.title: Unmarried men went to the vineyards to find a wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the girls danced in the vineyards. A תנא explains that a man without a wife would go there to find one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the daughters of ישראל go out and dance in the vineyards. A תנא taught: whoever had no wife would go there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the dancing in the vineyards. A תנא tells us the purpose of the event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only described girls dancing. The תנא adds the reason: it was a time for unmarried men to come and choose a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: a teacher of a ברייתא taught

phrases.english: The daughters of Israel go out and dance in the vineyards.
A tanna taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה, נִפְנֶה לְשָׁם.
phrases.english: One who has no wife would turn to there.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאוֹת וְחוֹלוֹת בַּכְּרָמִים. תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dancing in the vineyards was a gathering where unmarried men could find a wife.

steps.title: What the beautiful girls said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the girls of fine lineage. A ברייתא then lists what each group of girls said, starting with the beautiful ones, who told the men to look at beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the girls from fine families among them would say, 'Young man,' etc. תנו רבנן: What would the beautiful ones say? 'Set your eyes on beauty, because a wife is for beauty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and opens a ברייתא that goes through three groups of girls. This step gives the first group, the beautiful ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned only the girls of fine lineage. The ברייתא adds more groups. Each group points to its own strength, and the beautiful girls point to their looks.

phrases.aramaic: מְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן הָיוּ אוֹמְרוֹת: בָּחוּר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Those of distinguished lineage among them would say: 'Young man,' etc.
The Rabbis taught:
What would the beautiful ones among them say?
'Set your eyes on beauty,'
'for a wife is only for beauty.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן הָיוּ אוֹמְרוֹת: בָּחוּר וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the vineyard scene by telling us what the girls said to the men.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beautiful girls asked the men to choose based on beauty.

steps.title: What the girls from fine families said
steps.stepSummary: The girls of distinguished lineage told the men to look at family, because a wife is for having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would the girls from fine families say? 'Set your eyes on family, because a wife is for children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second group, the girls from distinguished families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These girls point to something lasting: the children inherit their mother's family background. So a good family matters more than looks.

phrases.english: What would those of distinguished lineage among them say?
'Set your eyes on family,'
'because a wife is only for children.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second item in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The girls of fine lineage asked the men to choose based on family, for the sake of the children.

steps.title: What the less attractive girls said
steps.stepSummary: The less attractive girls asked the men to marry them לשם שמים, as long as the men would adorn them with gold jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would the less attractive ones say? 'Make your choice for the sake of Heaven, as long as you adorn us with gold jewelry.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the third group, the girls who were not beautiful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These girls have neither looks nor famous families to point to. So they ask the man to marry for a pure reason, לשם שמים. They add, cleverly, that with nice jewelry after the wedding they will look lovely too.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's dancing was organized with care: everyone borrowed clothes so no poor girl was embarrassed, the clothes were immersed, and it was a chance for unmarried men to find a wife. Each group of girls pointed to its own strength: beauty, family, or marrying לשם שמים.
steps.confusionAlert: Lines like 'a wife is only for beauty' are what the girls themselves said to promote themselves. They are not a halachic ruling of the גמרא.

phrases.english: What would the unattractive ones among them say?
'Take your acquisition for the sake of Heaven,'
'provided that you adorn us with gold jewelry.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last item in the ברייתא, which closes the explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The less attractive girls asked to be chosen לשם שמים, as long as they would be adorned with gold.

steps.title: The future dance of the צדיקים in גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: עולא ביראה quotes רבי אלעזר: in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a dance for the צדיקים in גן עדן. He will sit among them, and each one will point to Him. The proof is a פסוק in ישעיה that says 'Behold, this is our God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא from the town of בירא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a dance for the צדיקים. He will sit among them in גן עדן, and every single one of them will point with his finger. The source is the פסוק: 'And it will be said on that day: Behold, this is our God, we hoped to Him and He will save us. This is ה׳, we hoped to Him. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the מסכת with a hopeful picture. It moves from the girls' dance in the vineyards to a future dance of the צדיקים around הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the word זה ('this') in the פסוק, which the פסוק says twice. You say 'this' when you point at something you can see. So the צדיקים will see הקדוש ברוך הוא so clearly that each one can point to Him, as if with a finger. The dance is a circle, and He sits in the middle, the same distance from every צדיק.

keyTerms.meaning: The future, the time of the final redemption
A dance, especially a circle dance
The Garden of Eden, the place of reward
Points with his finger, showing something he can clearly see
We hoped and waited for Him

steps.whyThisMatters: The מסכת deals with fasting, troubles and prayers for rain. It ends on purpose with joy and hope. The long waiting (קוינו לו) will end in clearly seeing הקדוש ברוך הוא and rejoicing in His ישועה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא בִּירָאָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Ulla of Bira'a said that Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: The attribution line, merged into this step

phrases.english: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will make a dance for the righteous,
and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden,
and each and every one will point with his finger,
as it says: "And it will be said on that day:
Behold, this is our God,
phrases.notes: The word 'this' is the proof for pointing

phrases.english: we hoped to Him and He will save us;
this is the Lord, we hoped to Him;
let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא בִּירָאָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It links to the dancing in the vineyards from the earlier steps and moves from that earthly dance to a future spiritual dance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will lead a dance of the צדיקים in גן עדן. He will be seen so clearly that each one can point to Him, as the פסוק says 'this is our God.'

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the פרק and מסכת תענית
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק בשלשה פרקים. It also announces that מסכת תענית is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק בשלשה פרקים, and מסכת תענית is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional closing line said when you finish a פרק, and here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך means 'we will return to you.' It is a promise not to forget this learning and to come back to it. The words וסליקא לה tell us that this was the last פרק of מסכת תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula for a פרק

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת תענית is full of fasting and prayers in hard times. It ends with the joyful promise that the צדיקים will one day dance around הקדוש ברוך הוא and point to Him, saying 'this is our God.'

phrases.english: We will return to you, "In three places"
phrases.notes: The name of the פרק, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: and Tractate Taanit is concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת right after the final אגדה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק בשלשה פרקים and all of מסכת תענית are complete, with the promise to return to this learning.
